doc.title: Mickey Roker interviewed by Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Hard bop and the thrill of playing in New York
summary: Roker calls hard bop heaven, recalling being a young married father with a day job who never dreamed of playing with his idols; his funniest story is the waltz jam session.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Let me ask you about that, ‘cause you talked about Horace Silver. First of all the hard bop period is like some of my favorite music. Tell me about how that music feels from the inside out.

Man it’s just heaven man. It’s strong and I was young man. You know we were all young guys you know, and it was beautiful man because it was so exciting for me, you know, because I never in my wildest imagination believed that I would be in New York playing with these guys I’d been looking at all my life you know. I always loved music you know, and I could always play the drums you know, but I never, you know I was married and I had two kids and I had to work a day job in the beginning. Until I went to New York. So I never dreamed that I would be playing with people like that I played with. So I was always excited man. To me it was like I died and went to heaven.

I wanted to ask you, do you have any little, funny little things that happened to you like on the bandstand or while you were traveling with a group? Little crazy things that the average person may not think has anything to do with the music, but eventually finds its way into the music.

Well that story I told about me playing in four-four and the music was in three-four, that’s about the funniest story I got you know. Because you know there are a lot of stories but I can’t think of one to tell you right now. Little funny stories.
